turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. Yeah, um, I guess... well, what really made me come in is just this whole situation at my job. I work as a buyer, doing wholesale and retail purchasing, so I deal with a lot of vendors and inventory for new product launches. It's a lot of responsibility, you know, making sure the allocations are right and everything comes in on time. But recently, I just... I can't shake the feeling that people at work, and even some of the outside vendors we buy from, are secretly tracking my buys. 

Like, they're monitoring every single purchase order I make and then going into the system behind my back and messing with the launch numbers. I know they're doing it just to make me look stupid. Like they want me to fail or look totally incompetent in front of management. It got so bad that I finally went to my supervisor about it, because obviously it's a huge issue if our numbers are being tampered with, and he sat me down and pulled up all these system reports. He spent like an hour going line by line, showing me how the reports don't prove that anyone is changing my numbers, and he kept saying everything matches my original inputs. 

But I just... I look at his screen, and I hear what he's saying, but I can't shake it. Even looking right at his reports, I just know they're doing it. It's like this whole coordinated effort to set me up, and no matter how many spreadsheets he prints out, it doesn't change what's actually happening. It's just really getting to me because I have to watch my back every single time I place an order now, and it's exhausting having to constantly check and re-check my work because I know someone is just waiting to tweak the data the second I log off.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that coworkers and vendors are tampering with their work to make them look incompetent, which persists even when presented with contradictory evidence by their supervisor.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the feeling that people are tampering with your work, have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah... actually, yeah, I have. And honestly, it's been really freaking me out lately because it happens when I know for an absolute fact I'm alone. Like, there's this one specific voice—it's a man's voice, kind of deep, and it sounds like he's standing right over my shoulder, just inches away. 

Sometimes I'll be in the back stockroom, you know, where we keep the overflow before it hits the retail floor, and it's usually pretty quiet back there except for the HVAC unit kicking on and off. I'll be pulling some boxes or checking the SKUs to make sure the receiving team didn't mess up the count—because like I said, I have to double-check everything now—and suddenly I'll hear him say, "Move faster, Scott." Just like that, clear as day. And I'll spin around, expecting to see one of the warehouse guys or my manager trying to sneak up and micromanage me again, but the aisle is completely empty. Nobody's there. I'll even walk down to the end of the row to check if someone is hiding, but it's just me. 

And it's not just at work either, which is the weirdest part. The other day I was driving back from this huge vendor meeting out in the suburbs. Traffic was awful, so I was already kind of stressed out about getting back to the office in time to input the new inventory, and I heard the exact same guy laughing from the backseat. He was just laughing at my picks, like he was mocking the purchase orders I had just finalized at the meeting, treating me like I didn't know what I was doing. I literally slammed on my brakes and looked in the rearview mirror, but my car was totally empty. I even pulled over to check the back. It's just... I don't get how a voice can be so loud and right next to my ear, criticizing my work, when there is physically no one else around. It just adds to this whole feeling that I'm being watched all the time, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes a persistent belief that he is being watched all the time and suspects coworkers or managers of sneaking up on him.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly confirms hearing a man's voice speaking to him and laughing at him when he is completely alone.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing these feelings about your coworkers and hearing this voice?
turns.patient_response:
Um, let me think... if I really trace it back to when I first noticed the numbers being off and when that guy started talking to me, it’s been roughly ten months now. Yeah, about ten months. 

I remember exactly because I had just turned 22 and we were right in the middle of prepping the big Q3 wholesale allocations. At first, you know, I just thought I was tired or maybe I fat-fingered a decimal point on the purchase orders. You stare at spreadsheets long enough and your eyes start to play tricks on you, right? But then it kept happening, and that’s when the voice started chiming in, right around the exact same time. 

For ten whole months, it’s just been this relentless cycle. I’ll go into work, think I have a handle on the inventory, and then I realize someone is tweaking the system behind my back, and almost immediately that guy is right over my shoulder telling me I'm too slow or that I'm messing up. You have no idea how incredibly draining it is to deal with this for almost a year. I mean, I even started keeping a physical paper notebook a few months ago just to write down my original inputs, because I realized this wasn't stopping and I needed hard proof. But even when I write it down, the voice just laughs at me, like I said, from the backseat of my car on the way home or when I'm alone in the stockroom. 

My supervisor acts like this is just some sudden stress thing because I finally brought it up to him, but he doesn't realize I've been carrying this for ten months. Ten months of constantly looking over my shoulder, constantly re-checking the SKUs, just waiting for them to sabotage me again. It's just a really long time to feel like you're completely under a microscope, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that coworkers are secretly tweaking the inventory system to sabotage them.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient describes hearing a voice that criticizes and laughs at them, even when they are completely alone in their car or the stockroom.

turns.doctor_question: During these past ten months, have there been any periods of time where your mood was so low that you felt hopeless or lost interest in everything, or conversely, periods where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, and felt like you were on top of the world?
turns.patient_response:
Hopeless? I mean, not really hopeless, because honestly I'm usually too busy trying to keep everything from falling apart to feel down. But that other thing you mentioned, the energy? Yeah, absolutely. It’s actually kind of intense, and it happens a lot. 

I get these... these stretches, I guess you'd call them, where my brain is just firing on all cylinders and I don't even feel tired. I'll wake up at like 3 AM and I'm just ready to go, already mapping out supply chains and vendor negotiations in my head. I get this amazing feeling during those weeks where I feel like the whole city is opening up for me, you know? Like I'm completely unstoppable and I can predict exactly what the retail market is going to do before anyone else even sees the trends. I'll walk into the office feeling like a million bucks, ready to completely revamp the entire inventory system, and I just feel so sharp. Like I'm ten steps ahead of everyone else in the building.

But the problem is—and this is where it gets really messy at work, especially on top of everything else I just told you about them messing with my numbers—when I'm in one of those zones, my patience is just totally gone. Like, zero. Negative patience. If I'm feeling that good and moving that fast, and then someone questions a purchase order I just drafted, or if my manager pulls me aside and tells me to slow down because I'm allocating too much budget too quickly... I just completely lose it. I snap way harder than I mean to. 

I mean, I'll just tear into them. I'll start going off about how they don't see the bigger picture and how they're holding the company back. Just the other week, one of the receiving guys asked a really basic question about a freight delivery window I set up, and I totally bit his head off right there on the loading dock. I couldn't help it. It’s just, when I’m operating on that level and feeling that electric, anyone getting in my way or telling me to pump the brakes just feels like an insult. So yeah, I definitely get those periods where I feel on top of the world, but it almost always turns into me blowing up at people over my POs.

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient reports waking up at 3 AM ready to go and not feeling tired, indicating a decreased need for sleep.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes increased goal-directed activity at work, such as mapping out supply chains and wanting to completely revamp the inventory system.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient admits to having zero patience and snapping or blowing up at coworkers over minor questions or instructions to slow down.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling down, stating they are too busy keeping things from falling apart to feel that way.
symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient explicitly denies feeling hopeless when asked by the doctor.

turns.doctor_question: During those periods where you feel like you're on top of the world and have that extra energy, do you still hear that man's voice and feel like your coworkers are messing with your work?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, absolutely. It’s not like one thing turns off when the other turns on, you know? It all just kind of... crashes together. Like, during those weeks when I’m in that zone, the times when I'm barely sleeping—maybe getting two or three hours a night, tops, but waking up feeling completely wired and ready to go—I’ll go into the office and I just cannot stop talking. I’ll be talking nonstop to anyone who will listen about the upcoming sneaker trends, because sneakers are my main category, right? I'll be cornering the merchandising guys by the breakroom, explaining exactly why the retro high-tops are going to completely dominate the Q4 sales over the standard runners, and I just feel completely untouchable at work. Like an absolute genius. Like nobody can touch my projections or my vision for the season. 

But the crazy thing is, even when I feel that powerful, even when I'm riding that massive wave of energy, I am still one hundred percent convinced that the vendors are manipulating the numbers behind my back. I'll be flying through the purchase orders, feeling like a rockstar, but I'll see a wholesale margin that looks even slightly off and I just know, I absolutely know, that they're tweaking the system to sabotage my buys and make me look bad. 

And the voice doesn't stop either. If anything, it just layers right on top of everything else. I’ll be standing there at my desk, buzzing with all this energy, typing out these massive allocation plans for the sneaker drops, and I'll hear him right over my shoulder again. He's still there, pushing me. Just saying, "move faster, move faster." It's like he knows I'm already going a hundred miles an hour, but he's still right there in my ear, demanding I go faster while I'm trying to outsmart the vendors. So yeah, they definitely happen at the exact same time, which just makes the whole thing so much more intense because I'm trying to manage this incredible high and revamp the whole department while also having to constantly defend myself against these vendors messing with my spreadsheets, and having this guy breathing down my neck the entire time... it's just a lot going on all at once, you know?

turns.doctor_question: Have there been any periods of at least two weeks where you felt completely stable in your mood—not high or low—but still experienced those thoughts about your coworkers and heard that voice?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, actually. That's... that's a really good question because I was just thinking about how weird that is. There was this stretch, maybe a couple of months ago, right after we got past the worst of the seasonal transition. Things at work had physically slowed down, and I actually felt... normal, I guess? Like, my mood was totally level. But even during a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally—like, actually getting a solid seven or eight hours a night instead of three—and not feeling like I was running the whole market, the other stuff didn't stop. 

You'd think if I was finally resting and not feeling all wired and aggressive, my brain would just hit the reset button, right? Like the paranoia or whatever my boss wants to call it would just fade out. But no. I still spent a few weeks during that exact same time believing people were tracking my buys. I would be sitting at my desk, totally calm, drinking my coffee, not feeling angry or hyped up at all, but I just knew they were monitoring my login times and tracking which vendors I was allocating the most budget to. I could just feel them watching my spreadsheets, waiting for me to finalize a PO so they could mess with the margins. 

And the voice didn't go away either. I remember specifically having to go into the back stockroom to audit this huge shipment of deadstock sneakers that had just come in. I was back there completely by myself, feeling totally fine, just doing inventory, and I was still hearing the voice in the stockroom. He was right there, just like always, making comments about how I was logging the boxes and telling me I was missing things. It's honestly so incredibly frustrating because it proves that it’s not just me being tired or stressed or hyped up on that energy wave. Even when I’m completely stable for weeks and feeling totally fine, they’re still tracking me and he’s still talking to me. It just never really gives me a break, even when my body finally does, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes a fixed belief that coworkers are tracking their buys and monitoring their login times to mess with their margins.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient reports hearing a voice making comments to them while they were completely alone in the stockroom.

symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient mentions being 'hyped up on that energy wave', implying periods of abnormally increased energy and activity.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient notes that outside of this stable period, they felt like they were 'running the whole market', indicating grandiosity.
